items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Jimmy Noon, he would play the 12 o'clock with Dr. Cook's 26 piece band. And then he would have his own band, Earl Hines and Bud Scott and Lawson Buford.

ctx.x: Well, I never did know whether she could have been married then as far as I knew. Yeah. But Joe had several women pianists. It seemed like there was more women pianists who played that type of music than the men. Now there was a pianist up there from here called Arthur Campbell too. He played with George Field in the spot. And later on, fellas like Tom Aladdin came up and Mutt was up there for a while. And they came up, I think Mary Mack, like Mary Mack had, they played at the Monogram Theater. And so they began…
Did you ever see Big Jim Coliseum around?

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: But I wouldn't put him in the same category as Earl Hines.

ctx.x: See what I'm talking about? So I mean I lived right across the street from Professor George Correa, and when I lived on Upper Line Street I was only two blocks from the Humphreys, and Mrs. Humphrey, old man Humphrey's daughter, taught me in the fourth grade at Tarly Farm School. And she taught us a little music there. And so she knew music and evidently I think she must have gotten from her father. And Willie Humphrey today, if he's still living, he reads a lot of music. His brother Earl was a trombone player,…
Well he's in the Eureka, the trumpet player, and he's the leader of the Eureka band, the brass band.
